title: Half the Size, Different Bugs
caption:
I've been reviewing AI code like it's junior code. That's the wrong instinct.

787,562 function pairs across Python, Java and C — each human function mined from open source, paired with an AI implementation written from the same docstring. The AI versions came out roughly half the size and half the branching, and the defects aren't worse versions of human defects. They're a different kind: human code concentrates the issues of mature codebases, AI code concentrates repetitive boilerplate.

The part I didn't expect: security doesn't move one way. More findings, and more severe ones, in Python and Java — but fewer high-severity memory-safety findings than the humans wrote in C. Worth saying it's a preprint under review, and the generators were GPT, DeepSeek-Coder and Qwen2.5-Coder, not the agent you ran this morning.

Which language do you trust it with?
